questions.prompt: What is the difference between a workflow and an agent, in Anthropic's words?

options.text: A workflow uses fixed code paths. An agent lets the model direct its own steps and tool use.
options.explanation: Right. The Anthropic engineering post defines workflows as predefined code paths, and agents as systems where the model dynamically directs its own process and tools.

options.text: A workflow always uses one model. An agent always uses two or more models at once.
options.explanation: Anthropic does not define agents by the number of models. The difference is who decides the steps.

options.text: A workflow makes images, while an agent makes only text because it cannot call a media tool.
options.explanation: Both can use tools, including media tools. The difference is who decides the steps.

questions.prompt: In OpenAI's agent loop, what happens when the model asks for a tool?

options.text: The run stops at once and the person must type the tool result in by hand
options.explanation: The loop does not stop there. The SDK runs the tool and continues.

options.text: The runner runs the tool, adds the result to the input, and calls the model again
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's loop runs the tool calls, appends the results, and re-runs, until the model gives a final answer.

options.text: The tool call is saved for later and is only run once the model gives its final answer
options.explanation: Tool calls run inside the loop, before the final answer. The result goes back to the model.

questions.prompt: Why is the cost of an agent run hard to predict?

options.text: The vendor hides the price of each model call until the end of the month
options.explanation: The reason is the loop itself, not hidden prices.

options.text: Agents always cost the same, so the real problem is only the cost of the tools they call
options.explanation: Costs vary with the number of loops. Google's range is wide, from 100k to 3M tokens.

options.text: The model picks the number of loops, so the call count is unknown when you start
options.explanation: Right. The Gemini API docs say one managed-agent interaction can trigger multiple reasoning loops, typically 100k to 3M tokens.
